title: The Scholar's Revelation
subtitle: He is not sleeping. He is suffering.

customObject.name: hologram of R'lyeh
customObject.description: a projected model of the sunken city — wrong angles, tilted spires, a sick green-violet shimmer

script.note: MAP: st_pancras_new_church_crypt — a hidden sanctuary below the city. Ancient texts, arcane instruments, and one impossible hologram turning slowly in the dark. Night.

script.text: There you are. Good. My readings are getting worse — the psychic tremors from R'lyeh are intensifying.

script.note: The Re-Architect approaches the hologram. Its geometry is wrong — angles that subtract instead of add.

script.text: I thought the Sleeper was merely dreaming. That his dreams drove men mad, and that was the whole of it.
That's the myth. The convenient lie. The truth is far more tragic — he is not merely sleeping. He is suffering.

R'lyeh is not a throne. It is a prison. And it is a prison built from his own despair — every drowned street of it shaped by the torment of the being it holds. It is anathema to him. It is slowly poisoning him.
You're telling me the monster hates his cage — not the world outside it.

The lashing out of a tormented god is not the same thing as evil. Read the fragments again: his waking dreams are not of conquest. They are of escape. Of an environment of peace, order, purpose. He dreams, in his way, of home.
Then what do we do with that? You can't banish a being like him. And no one has ever slain one.
We do neither. We heal his world.

script.note: She pulls a scarred old volume from the shelf — a copy of a copy of the Book of the Dead — and lays it open beside the hologram.

script.text: The old Egyptians understood something we forgot: that a place can be built to lift a spirit, or to crush one. Architectural magics. Resonant geometry. The texts never name the Sleeper — but they teach exactly what his prison lacks.

The rituals are scattered — forgotten tombs, forbidden libraries, drowned observatories. Piece by piece we can re-architect R'lyeh itself. Straighten what maddens. Light what despairs. Turn the tomb into a sanctuary.
And the Sleeper? When his walls stop screaming at him — what wakes up?

That is the question no prophecy answers. But I believe what wakes in a healed house is not what raged in a ruined one. We are not saving a monster. We are meeting, for the first time, whoever he actually is.

To begin, we need a guide — the texts call them Risen Spirits. Enlightened echoes of civilisations that learned to build in harmony. The first is bound to a place where the desert sands meet forgotten waters.

script.note: OBJECTIVE — a new waypoint appears: THE SUNKEN OASIS OF KHEM. Uncover the first fragment of the Ritual of Harmonious Geomancy and summon the Risen Spirit.

script.text: The Sunken Oasis of Khem. Then that's where we start — not with a sword. With a blueprint.
With a blueprint — and with the strangest act of mercy this world has ever attempted. Go carefully, Architect. Even a kindness can wake something.
